key_insight: Cedalion is an open-source Python framework that unifies model-based and data-driven analysis of multimodal fNIRS & DOT, enabling reproducible, end-to-end neuroimaging workflows from lab experiments to real-world/ wearable data.
problem_solved: Addresses fragmented toolchains and poor interoperability in fNIRS/DOT analysis, which hinder reproducibility, scaling to multimodal and wearable data, and integration with modern ML workflows.
method: Modular Python API providing unified preprocessing, artifact correction, DOT reconstruction, and multimodal synchronization.
Built-in support for ML-ready pipelines: feature extraction, cross-validation, simulation/benchmarking, and reproducible notebooks/workflows.
Extensible plugin architecture and standardized data formats to enable real-time and offline analysis across lab and everyday recordings.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, Cedalion lowers the barrier to apply modern ML methods to fNIRS/DOT by providing standardized, reproducible data pipelines and tools for benchmarking models on multimodal, wearable neuroimaging datasets.
visual_elements: High-level pipeline diagram: acquisition → preprocessing → DOT reconstruction → feature extraction → ML/visualization
Modular architecture graphic showing core modules (I/O, preprocessing, reconstruction, ML) and plugin/extensions
Before/after comparison chart: fragmented toolchain vs Cedalion unified workflow (time-to-result, reproducibility, interoperability)
Example outputs: reconstructed DOT brain map + aligned multimodal time-series (EEG, motion) as a small panel
paper_title: Cedalion Tutorial: A Python-based framework for comprehensive analysis of multimodal fNIRS & DOT from the lab to the everyday world
paper_authors: E. Middell, L. Carlton, S. Moradi, T. Codina, T. Fischer
